newsitem.title: UK: UK govt confirms BoE free to set interest rates.
newsitem.headline: UK govt confirms BoE free to set interest rates.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government confirmed on Wednesday it would give the Bank of England operational responsibility for setting interest rates.

Queen Elizabeth, in a speech to officially open the new parliamentary session, said the measure, announced last week, was aimed "to deliver price stability and support for the government's overall economic policy, within a framework of enhanced accountability."
A government note accompanying the speech said the Bank will set short-term interest rates to achieve the government's target of low and stable inflation of 2.5 percent or less.
A bill will be introduced to amend the Bank of England Act 1946, setting up the new monetary framework.
